clue.text: It promotes digestion of vehicle in drink

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the vehicle sits inside the word for drink

parts.note: to bib is an old verb meaning to drink, as in 'wine-bibber'
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Some digestive aid comes from a car steeped in liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: BICARB is short for bicarbonate of soda, taken to settle indigestion; 'bib' is an old word for tippling.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarbonate of soda is a traditional antacid swallowed to ease an upset stomach after eating.

clue.text: Identifying condition of quoted number given help

annotationWithheld.why: 'Identifying condition of quoted number given help (10)' for DIAGNOSTIC: 'Identifying condition' defines it, but no parse of 'of quoted number given help' building DIAGNOSTIC could be found, and no blog for this puzzle turned up
annotationWithheld.clue: Identifying condition of quoted number given help

clue.text: Want to get into fortress — but only so far!

indicators.note: 'get into' says the word for want is placed inside the fortress

parts.note: a keep is the central stronghold of a castle
to want is to need

explanation.surface: A besieger wants to enter a fortress but gets only part way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but only so far!' is the definition: wading knee-deep you are in, but only up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knee-deep means immersed to a limited depth, partly in rather than fully.

clue.text: Reviewer whose leader takes two steps back in type of acid

indicators.note: the letter shifts two places toward the front of the word, as if stepping back toward the start

parts.note: citric acid is the acid in lemons

explanation.surface: A critic's leader retreats two paces inside some acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whose leader' points to the first letter of 'Reviewer', R; moving the R of CITRIC two places forward gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic is someone who writes reviews of plays, books or films.

clue.text: Can't hope to be resurrected by monument

indicators.note: resurrected letters are brought back to life in a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone despairs of being brought back from the dead by a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be resurrected' rearranges the eight letters of CANT HOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a memorial monument to people buried elsewhere, such as war dead.

clue.text: Progress slowly with polar explorer (incomplete: unfinished)

parts.note: to inch is to move forward very slowly

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Lawrence Oates died on Scott's Antarctic expedition of 1912

explanation.surface: Slow progress with a polar explorer leaves the job incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts the final S from OATES, Captain Oates of Scott's ill-fated South Pole party.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means just begun and not fully formed, hence incomplete or undeveloped.

clue.text: Indicator of how to finish letters?

definitions.meaning: a sign or pointer showing the way
to end a letter you sign it and then put it in the post

explanation.surface: A guide to rounding off one's correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost points the way; finishing a letter means signing it then sending it by post.

clue.text: Not initially unwilling to curse

indicators.note: 'not initially' drops the first letter of the word

parts.note: loath means reluctant or unwilling

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant at first is now willing to swear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' removes the L from LOATH.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can be a swear word or profanity, the same as a curse.

clue.text: Legendary friar given a bit of plastic surgery

definitions.meaning: the jolly friar among Robin Hood's band of outlaws
a cosmetic operation that tightens skin

explanation.surface: A friar from folklore undergoes a cosmetic procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar Tuck is Robin Hood's companion; a tuck is a surgical tightening of loose skin.

clue.text: Fine beverage inducing drunken trance

indicators.note: drunken suggests letters reeling out of order

explanation.surface: A drink so good it sends you into a stupor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges TRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the gods, so any delicious drink can be called nectar.

clue.text: Unsophisticated GI reacts oddly

indicators.note: oddly means the letters behave strangely and are reordered

explanation.surface: An American soldier behaves strangely, showing a lack of polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges GI REACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrestic means rural or rustic, hence uncouth and unsophisticated.

clue.text: Refractory book about currency units

indicators.note: 'about' means the book's word goes around the currency units

parts.note: a tome is a large book
roubles are Russian money

explanation.surface: A stubborn volume concerned with money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal here, not 'concerning'; 'Refractory' means stubborn, not heat-resistant.
explanation.definitionFit: Refractory and troublesome both describe someone stubborn and hard to manage.

clue.text: Raised student with half 19 collecting strange paintings outside college

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the whole sequence is read from the bottom up

parts.note: L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

indicators.note: 'collecting' says the half of the other entry holds the next pieces

parts.note: the first half of the guitarist entry at 19 down
rum is British slang for odd or strange
art means paintings

explanation.surface: A student and half a guitarist gather odd pictures beyond the campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns the whole assembly upside down in this down entry; 'collecting' wraps the first half of the 19-down answer round the odd paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Extramural means beyond the walls of a university, like courses for non-resident students.

clue.text: Thus medic pinches US brother's hat

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: pinches means grips, so the medic holds the brother inside

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
Brer is a Southern US dialect form of brother, as in Brer Rabbit

explanation.surface: A doctor steals an American's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinches' looks like theft but means grips, holding the brother inside the medic.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a wide-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Facing prospect of an excavation with nothing to lose — it's beneath one

indicators.note: 'to lose' says the letter for nothing is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: someone about to be dug at is 'in for a dig'
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone about to dig has nothing to lose, though the task is beneath them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' removes O from IN FOR A DIG; INFRA DIG is short for Latin infra dignitatem.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra dig, short for infra dignitatem, describes something beneath a person's dignity.

clue.text: Saucepan's ready for use — take it and see what happens!

definitions.text: take it and see what happens!

parts.note: a pot is a saucepan, with the 's as 'is'
a pan that is hot is ready for cooking

explanation.surface: The pan has heated up, so try cooking and see what comes of it.
explanation.walkthrough: POT'S HOT reads as a sentence; a potshot is a random try with no careful aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A potshot is a random, unaimed attempt, fired off just to see the result.

clue.text: Where to get care if 7 slip out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 7 down is a word for a curse or vow

explanation.surface: Where you get treatment if you let a swear word escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges OATH (the answer to 7 down) with SLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital is the institution where patients receive medical care.

clue.text: Losing energy, upset honeypot in high wind

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A gale knocks over a honey jar and saps your strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing' takes E out of HONEYPOT; 'upset' rearranges the remaining HONYPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A typhoon is a tropical cyclone with violent high winds.

clue.text: Stiffener and preservative in court

parts.note: starch stiffens collars and cloth
amber is fossil resin that preserves trapped insects

explanation.surface: A stiffening agent and preservative go to law.
explanation.walkthrough: The Star Chamber was an English court abolished in 1641, known for arbitrary rulings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Star Chamber was a historic English court, now a byword for arbitrary tribunals.

clue.text: Guitarist (North American) holding his credit card up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top
holding means the North American abbreviation goes around the card

parts.note: Amex is the American Express card

explanation.surface: A North American guitarist keeps his credit card raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' wraps the abbreviation round the card; 'up' turns the result around in this down entry. 'his' is only linking surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Axeman is slang for a guitarist, from 'axe' as slang for a guitar.

clue.text: Couple with something on the agenda

definitions.meaning: two people in a romantic relationship are called this
a single point on a list for discussion

explanation.surface: A pair with business to discuss.
explanation.definitionFit: An item can mean a romantic couple, or a single entry on a list.

clue.text: Older relation — nearly 1,000!

indicators.note: 'nearly' says the last letter is lost

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: An elderly relative almost a thousand years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the D from GRAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Gran is short for grandmother, an older family member.

clue.text: End of American semester?

parts.note: a semester is an academic term
something in the US is American, so 'in US' stands for it

explanation.surface: The close of a US college semester.
explanation.walkthrough: An American semester is a 'term in US'.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is an endpoint, especially the last stop on a transport line.

clue.text: Key provided guidance about information

indicators.note: 'about' says the guiding word goes around the information

parts.note: led means guided
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An important person guided others with information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the guiding word round the information; 'Key' is a noun, as on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is the key explaining the symbols on a map or chart.

clue.text: Capital once also invested in language

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, as money is put into something

parts.note: Malay is the language of Malaysia
and means also

explanation.surface: A former capital put money into a language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' puts the conjunction inside the language; Mandalay was the royal capital of Burma before 1885.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandalay was the last royal capital of Burma, now Myanmar, before British annexation.

clue.text: Woman's returned girl's first garment

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the woman's name is read backwards

parts.note: Nora is a woman's name, with the possessive giving S

indicators.note: first means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A woman has given back her daughter's first piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns NORAS into SARON; 'first' adds G from girl's.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a wrapped skirt-like garment worn in South-East Asia.
